q: How do you build and use Helm OCI dependencies and chart caching in air-gapped or restricted environments?
a: Air-gapped clusters cannot reach public registries, so everything is mirrored and resolved internally. The process starts in a connected staging area where approved charts and images are pulled, scanned and reviewed, then copied into an internal OCI registry with tools such as helm pull and helm push, oras, skopeo or crane, or a registry replication feature in Harbor, preserving versions and digests. Chart dependencies in Chart.yaml point at the internal registry, so dependency build resolves offline, and Chart.lock keeps exact versions. Image references in values are rewritten to the internal registry, using global image registry values, or a post-renderer, or a mirror configured on the container runtime. For a fully disconnected network, charts and images are exported into a signed bundle, transferred over an approved medium, verified against signatures and digests, then imported. Vendoring dependency archives in Git removes registry reliance for builds. The Helm cache and config directories in CI are set to known paths, so runs are reproducible without network calls. Updates follow a regular cadence with the same scan and approval steps, and an inventory records which versions are present.
f: How do images get rewritten to the internal registry?
p: Mirror reviewed charts and images into an internal OCI registry, point dependencies and image values at it, keep Chart.lock and vendored archives for offline builds, transfer signed bundles for fully disconnected networks, verify digests and signatures and refresh on a regular approved cadence.
cmds: helm pull oci://public.example/charts/app --version 1.4.0 && helm push app-1.4.0.tgz oci://registry.internal/charts
tip: Say mirror, pin, verify, rewrite image registries.
